standard_prerequisites.name: A finite type module flat at a point is finitely presented there, and a finitely presented module can be manufactured from the stalk
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-finite-type-flat-at-point-local (proof line 4121); Algebra, label algebra-lemma-construct-fp-module-from-stalk (proof line 4123)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a finitely presented module F' with a map to F that is an isomorphism at the chosen point, which is the first construction of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Openness of flatness and surjectivity of a map of finite type modules detected on a stalk
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Morphisms, label more-morphisms-theorem-openness-flatness (proof line 4129); Modules, label modules-lemma-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk (proof line 4133); Algebra, label algebra-lemma-NAK (proof line 4135)
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes F' flat over the base after shrinking the source and the map from F' to F surjective after shrinking again, so that the proof is reduced to controlling the kernel.

standard_prerequisites.name: Weakly associated points of a tensor product with a pulled back sheaf, finiteness of the associated points of a fibre, and weakly associated primes of a submodule
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-bourbaki-finite-type-general-base (proof line 4137); Divisors, labels divisors-lemma-finite-ass (proof line 4145) and divisors-lemma-ses-weakly-ass (proof line 4153); Algebra, labels algebra-lemma-silly (proof line 4147) and Divisors, label divisors-lemma-weakly-ass-zero (proof line 4158)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first bounds the weakly associated points of F' by the finitely many weakly associated points of the base times the associated points of the fibres, the second makes those finite, the third lets the weakly associated points be assumed to specialize into the chosen point, and the last two are used to conclude that a module whose weakly associated points are all generalizations of a point at which it vanishes is zero.

core_obligations: Localise the problem: for a point x where F is flat over S it suffices to find an open neighbourhood on which F restricts to a flat finitely presented module, so one may take X and S affine; since the stalk of F at x is finitely presented, construct a finitely presented module F' mapping to F by an isomorphism at x, note F' is flat at x, use openness of flatness to assume F' flat over S after shrinking X, and use that F is of finite type to assume the map surjective after shrinking again (proof lines 4114-4135).

Control the weakly associated points: by the general base weak Bourbaki lemma the weakly associated points of F' over X lie in the union over the weakly associated points of the base of the associated points of the fibres; the former set is finite by hypothesis and each of the latter is finite, so the weakly associated points of F' form a finite set, and after shrinking X once more one may assume they all specialize into the chosen point x (proof lines 4136-4150).

Kill the kernel: the weakly associated points of the kernel K of the map F' -> F are contained in those of F' by the weak associated points of a short exact sequence, while the map is an isomorphism at every generalization of x, so the weakly associated points of K are empty and the kernel vanishes, which finishes the proof that the restriction of F to the neighbourhood is finitely presented and flat (proof lines 4150-4159).
proof_roadmap: Replace the module by a finitely presented model and make it flat and the map onto the original surjective (proof lines 4114-4135).

Bound the weakly associated points of the model by the weakly associated points of the base and the associated points of the fibres, and shrink so that they all specialize into the chosen point (proof lines 4136-4150).
Show the kernel vanishes because its weakly associated points would have to be empty (proof lines 4150-4159).
difficulty_reason: The theorem is the non Noetherian form of openness of flatness: for a locally finitely presented morphism and a finite type module, provided the weakly associated points of the base are locally finite, the flat locus is open and the module restricts there to a finitely presented flat module (statement lines 4096-4112, tag 05IK). The proof is a real construction: it manufactures a finitely presented model of the stalk that maps to the module, makes it flat over the base and the map surjective after shrinking, bounds the weakly associated points of that model by the weakly associated points of the base times the associated points of the fibres, shrinks the source so that those points specialize into the chosen point, and then shows the kernel vanishes because its weakly associated points would have to be empty. The weakly associated point bookkeeping is the substance, so the claim is H2.
